title: Accelerated Multiple Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Multi-objective Distributional Optimization
claim: Our accelerated variant drives the convergence metric to zero far faster than the baseline across all step sizes and both discretizations.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, shaded std bands, shared legend style
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the x-axis 'Iterations' (0 to 1000) and the y-axis 'GradNorm'. Panel (a), titled 'SVGD-based variants', shows MWGraD-SVGD as dotted curves and A-MWGraD-SVGD as solid curves, each at three learning rates (0.001 blue, 0.005 green, 0.01 red). Panel (b), titled 'Blob-based variants', uses the same encoding for the Blob versions. Shaded bands show the standard deviation. The solid accelerated curves fall to near zero within about 100 to 300 iterations. The dotted baseline curves decay slowly. The slowest baseline, blue at lr=0.001, is still far from zero at 1000 iterations. Each panel has a large legend in the upper right. The panels are labeled (a) and (b) below. The eye goes first to the steep red and green solid drops at the left of each plot.
caption: Convergence comparison: (a) SVGD-based variants, (b) Blob-based variants. The plot show mean and standard deviation of $\operatorname{GradNorm}$ over 1000 iterations with three different step sizes of $\eta=0.001, 0.005, 0.01$.
abstract: We study multi-objective optimization over probability distributions in Wasserstein space. Recently, Nguyen et al. (2025) introduced Multiple Wasserstein Gradient Descent (MWGraD) algorithm, which exploits the geometric structure of Wasserstein space to jointly optimize multiple objectives. Building on this approach, we propose an accelerated variant, A-MWGraD, inspired by Nesterov's acceleration. We analyze the continuous-time dynamics and establish convergence to weakly Pareto optimal points in probability space. Our theoretical results show that A-MWGraD achieves a convergence rate of O(1/t^2) for geodesically convex objectives and O(e^{-\sqrtÎ²t}) for $Î²$-strongly geodesically convex objectives, improving upon the O(1/t) rate of MWGraD in the geodesically convex setting. We further introduce a practical kernel-based discretization for A-MWGraD and demonstrate through numerical experiments that it consistently outperforms MWGraD in convergence speed and sampling efficiency on multi-target sampling tasks.
